group_structure: Commercial bank with an Islamic window (NBF Islamic). Two wholly owned support subsidiaries: NBF Financial Services FZC (Fujairah Free Zone, support services) and NBF Markets (Cayman) Limited (vehicle for FX and derivative transactions with counterparties under ISDA). No asset-management or brokerage subsidiary.

footprint: UAE only: 15 branches in Fujairah, Abu Dhabi, Dubai, Sharjah and Ras Al Khaimah (30 Jun 2026); network also includes 74 independent ATMs and CDMs (2025 annual report).
customer_segments: Corporate and institutional, business banking (SME to mid-market), treasury clients; retail with tiered propositions NBF Preferred, NBF Priority and NBF Al Samy (HNW, net worth 1m+); Islamic customers via NBF Islamic. Stated focus: 'UAE-wide premium bank for SMEs to mid-market businesses ... and affluent to high-net-worth individual segments'.
business_lines: Corporate & institutional banking, business banking, treasury and markets (NBF Markets, NBFX e-FX platforms), trade finance, retail banking (accounts, cards, loans, insurance, investment solutions), NBF Islamic window. Retail is small: H1 2026 retail operating income AED 105.7m of AED 1,381m total.

capabilities.wealth_summary: NBF is mainly a corporate and SME bank (retail was AED 105.7m of AED 1.38bn operating income in H1 2026), but its 2025 annual report names 'affluent to high-net-worth individual segments' as a strategic focus and says a digital wealth management platform will be implemented in 2026 (vendor not named). Retail tiers are NBF Preferred (salary AED 10k or AED 100k–350k balance), NBF Priority (salary 40k, 350k in deposits and/or investments, or mortgage above 2.5m; dedicated RM) and NBF Al Samy for net worth of 1m+ (promoted in a Jul 2025 campaign). Investment Solutions are RM-led: execution services (bonds, equity and fixed-income mutual funds, ETFs), non-discretionary advisory strategies and discretionary managed model portfolios built from third-party managers. No in-app investing, own funds, structured products for individuals or Islamic investment products were found. No AUM is disclosed.

segments.name: NBF Preferred
segments.eligibility: Minimum salary AED 10,000, or average balance AED 100,000–350,000 in deposits or equivalent, or mortgage up to AED 2.5m

segments.name: NBF Priority
segments.eligibility: Monthly salary 40,000+, or average balance 350,000 in deposits and/or investments, or mortgage above 2.5m (currency not stated on page; AED implied)

segments.name: NBF Al Samy
segments.eligibility: Net worth of 1 million or more; Jul–Aug 2025 campaign required minimum average monthly balance of 1 million for three months

private_banking.detail: No private-banking unit. HNW clients are served through NBF Al Samy (net worth 1m+) and Priority relationship managers; strategy targets 'affluent to high-net-worth individual segments' (2025 annual report).

asset_management.detail: No asset-management subsidiary (only NBF Financial Services FZC and NBF Markets (Cayman) Ltd). Model portfolios use 'best-in-class asset managers' (third party).

brokerage.detail: RM-led 'Investment Execution Services' for bonds, equity and fixed-income mutual funds, ETFs and other securities. Website footer cites a Capital Markets Authority (CMA) licence no. 20200000222. No online or app brokerage found.

digital_investing.detail: NBF Direct app (UAE Pass login, AI-enabled self-service) shows no investing features. The 2025 annual report states a digital wealth management platform will be implemented in 2026.

advisory.detail: Non-discretionary tailored multi-asset strategies proposed by the bank, with the client making final decisions; risk tolerance questionnaire and RM guidance.

discretionary.detail: 'Discretionary Managed Model Portfolios' — multi-asset, globally diversified (equities, bonds, cash) through third-party asset managers, matched to risk profiles.

model_portfolios_robo.detail: Discretionary model portfolios by risk profile (RM-delivered, not robo). No digital/robo channel found.

funds_platform.detail: Global equity and fixed-income mutual funds and ETFs offered via execution and advisory services; fund houses and platform provider not named.

structured_products.detail: Not listed among retail investment offerings. Treasury provides bespoke cross-asset derivative and market-risk solutions mainly to corporate clients (annual report).

private_markets.detail: No private-markets or alternatives offering found.

islamic_wealth.detail: NBF Islamic window offers deposits and financing (Islamic financing AED 5.1bn, deposits AED 4.9bn at H1 2026) but no Shariah-compliant investment products were found on investment pages.

opportunities: Plans to implement a digital wealth management platform in 2026; vendor not disclosed (S4 p.12).
New strategic focus on 'affluent to high-net-worth individual segments' alongside SMEs (S4 p.14); Priority and Al Samy tiers exist but have no digital investing (S10, S12).
Offers discretionary model portfolios and advisory only through RMs; no in-app investing, private markets or Islamic investment products (S9, S8).
barriers: Small retail franchise: retail operating income AED 105.7m in H1 2026 (down 10.3%), about 48,000 customers in total (S19, S4).
Corporate/SME-led bank; technology spend focused on core banking, cloud and cyber (S14).
Islamic window has no investment shelf, so any Islamic wealth offering would start from zero (S19, S8).
incumbent_vendors: Accenture LearnVantage / Udacity — AI workforce training only (S13)
